description:
The cps5_small.gdt dataset (Current Population Survey wage data, 1200 observations) is loaded in Gretl. Variables include: 'wage' (hourly earnings), 'educ' (years of education), 'exper' (years of potential experience), 'expersq' (experience squared), 'female' (=1 if female), 'black' (=1 if Black), 'metro' (=1 if metropolitan area), 'south' (=1 if southern region), 'midwest', 'west'.

A wage researcher needs to rigorously assess whether a log-wage Mincer equation is correctly specified. Your task:
1. Estimate a log-wage OLS regression: ln(wage) ~ educ + exper + expersq + female + black + metro + south
2. Run the RESET test (Ramsey's Regression Equation Specification Error Test) to check for omitted nonlinearities or functional form misspecification
3. Test for heteroskedasticity using both the Breusch-Pagan (BP) test and the White test
4. If heteroskedasticity is detected, re-estimate with heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC/robust) standard errors
5. Save all results to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/wage_diagnostics.txt

Gretl is open with cps5_small.gdt loaded.
